property_summary: For any caller and any payable amount, after go(...) returns the reference implementation always forwards all contract balance to owner (so address(c).balance == 0), whereas the mutant that uses call to send remaining balance can fail and leave funds in the contract for some adversarial callee behavior (so address(c).balance != 0).

For every call to go(...) the reference C always forwards any remaining contract balance to owner so address(c).balance == 0 after the call; the mutant replaces transfer with a low-level call that can fail for a malicious callee and thus can leave funds in the contract (address(c).balance != 0) for some inputs.

For any caller and any payable amount, calling go(...) on the correct contract always results in the contract having zero balance afterwards (it always forwards remaining balance to owner successfully); the mutant can leave non-zero balance when the owner’s receive/call deliberately reverts, so there exists an input (an owner that rejects payments) that makes address(c).balance != 0 after go.

For every caller and payable amount, the reference contract C always ends a successful go(...) call with address(c).balance == 0 (it always forwards remaining balance to owner via transfer); the mutant that uses a low-level call to send remaining balance can fail when owner rejects payments, causing address(c).balance != 0 for some owner behavior.
